set.st: Robbers of the Grass Lake bank fled to a hotel off Wolf Lake Road; police recovered most of the loot, but about $1,300 in gold and silver was never found. A Jackson paper a week later said the evidence pointed to someone picking the money up at the lakeside cottage during the gunfight, so a roadside cache is doubtful. Pin is on Mack Island, the knoll at the E end of Wolf Lake (the 1920 gunfight cottage site), not the spot itself.
set.t: Later report (4 Aug 1920) suggests the coins were pocketed at the cottage, not cached. Wet ground along the 1920 getaway route was never searched. Access: cottage lots: private, permission.
set.pl: Mack Island = the knoll at the E end of Wolf Lake (Mack Island Rd); cottage site of the 1920 gunfight.
pinev: Site-level: no true island exists today, but the USGS topo shows a wooded knoll at the E end of Wolf Lake, joined to the N shore by low wet ground and reached by Mack Island Rd: very likely the 1920 "Mack Island" where the gang was cornered (about 300 m).

tw-mi-bellevue-dolph-stumps.st: Tale: about $15,000 in gold stolen from a county treasurer before the Civil War was buried by four robbers on a river bank, and a map was made; a detective once asked the county for leave to dig and never came back.
src: JCP 1914-02-12 p8 (second local account: digging behind the swamp near the river on the same farm)
